title: Anthropic Secures $93.5 B Funding Round, Underwriters Snap Up Greenshoe Overallotment – CNBC Report
body:
Anthropic, the San Francisco‑based artificial‑intelligence firm founded by former OpenAI researchers, closed its landmark initial public offering on Friday after underwriters exercised a full greenshoe option, pushing the total proceeds to roughly $93.5 billion. The company sold 1.127 billion shares at $83 each, marking the largest U.S. equity debut for an AI‑focused business and the biggest IPO in the sector since the 2021 wave that saw several generative‑AI startups go public.

The greenshoe, a standard “overallotment” provision that allows underwriters to purchase up to 15 percent additional shares to stabilize the price, was fully taken up by the syndicate. This move not only underscored strong investor demand but also added roughly 169 million extra shares to the offering, expanding Anthropic’s market capitalization to well over $150 billion at the close of trading. The firm’s shares opened at $85.20, modestly above the IPO price, before settling at $84.70 by the end of the day, suggesting that the market has already begun to price in the company’s long‑term growth prospects.

Anthropic’s IPO arrives at a pivotal moment for the AI industry. While rivals such as OpenAI remain privately held, and others like Nvidia have benefited from a surge in AI‑related hardware demand, Anthropic’s public listing provides a rare benchmark for valuing pure‑play AI software companies. Analysts note that the $83 price tag reflects a premium of roughly 30 percent over the company’s last private valuation, signalling confidence in its flagship Claude models and the firm’s roadmap toward enterprise‑grade, safety‑focused AI solutions. The capital raised will fund an aggressive expansion plan, including the rollout of next‑generation language models, a broadened partnership network with cloud providers, and the recruitment of talent to bolster research and compliance capabilities.

The underwriting team—led by a consortium of Wall Street heavyweights—has been lauded for its swift execution amid a volatile macro environment. With inflationary pressures, tightening monetary policy, and geopolitical uncertainties still casting shadows over equity markets, the ability to secure near‑full subscription at a high price point is a testament to the “AI fever” that continues to grip institutional investors. Moreover, the robust greenshoe uptake hints that the underwriters anticipate continued upward momentum, a sentiment echoed by several buy‑side firms that have upgraded Anthropic to a “buy” rating, citing its differentiated safety architecture and growing enterprise pipeline.

Nonetheless, the IPO is not without risks. Critics point to the nascent nature of revenue streams for many AI developers, where monetization often hinges on high‑margin API usage and large‑scale licensing deals that can be fickle. Competition is intensifying, with cloud giants integrating their own large language models and startups racing to carve out niche verticals. Additionally, regulatory scrutiny over AI ethics, data privacy, and potential misuse could impose compliance costs that erode margins. Investors will be watching closely how Anthropic balances rapid product rollout with responsible AI governance—a factor that could influence both its brand reputation and its bottom line.

Looking ahead, Anthropic’s successful debut sets a new bar for AI IPOs and could pave the way for other private AI firms to seek public capital. The infusion of nearly $94 billion gives the company a formidable war chest to accelerate research, expand globally, and cement its position as a leader in safe, scalable AI. As the market digests the implications of this historic offering, the next few quarters will reveal whether Anthropic can translate its lofty valuation into sustainable growth, and whether the broader AI sector can sustain the enthusiasm that propelled this record‑breaking float.
